args.text:
Strategy brain (v1, written before game 1; no game results yet).

Placement phase:
- Prefer points that create a two-in-line with an open third point (forcing threats), and always block an opponent's open two-in-line immediately unless we can close our own mill first.
- Prefer junction points with 3-4 neighbours (5, 11, 14, 20, and the middle-ring midpoints 8, 12, 13, 17) over corners early; corners on outer ring are easier to trap.
- Keep pieces mobile: avoid placements that leave our pieces with no free neighbour.

Mill use:
- When closing a mill, remove an opponent piece that is part of a potential mill (two-in-line or blocker of our open line) and not in a mill; prefer pieces that are mobile/central.

Movement phase:
- Shuttle a piece between two points to re-form a mill (open/close mill) when the opponent cannot block the vacated point.
- Watch for opponent mill threats each turn: check every line where they have two pieces and third point is reachable by a piece of theirs in one move.
- With 3 pieces left, jumping is allowed; use it to create double threats.

Draw handling: avoid repeating positions three times when ahead; avoid 40 turns with no mill when we are behind in material.

Team process: captain proposes, others vote with a concrete reason; check the board before every proposal (move numbers: place = point; move = from*100+to; removal = point).

args.text:
Strategy brain (v1, drafted before game 1; no game results yet).

Opening (placement phase):
- Prefer junction points with 4 neighbours (5, 11, 14, 20) and the middle-ring points (8, 12, 13, 17). Corners (1, 3, 22, 24) have only 2 neighbours and get boxed in easily.
- Build two-in-a-row threats that can become mills in two directions at once.
- Always block an opponent two-in-a-row on an open line immediately, unless we can close our own mill this turn.

Middle game (moving phase):
- Keep pieces mobile. Avoid moves that leave our pieces with no free neighbour.
- Open and re-close mills (shuttle a piece between a mill point and an adjacent free point) when the opponent cannot block the gap.
- Count the opponent's one-move mill threats each turn before moving.

Removals:
- Remove opponent pieces that are not in mills (only mill pieces when all are in mills).
- Prefer removing a piece that is part of an opponent two-in-a-row or that blocks our own mill line; prefer pieces that can move freely.

Endgame:
- At 3 pieces we can fly: look for a double threat (two open lines that both need one more piece).
- Watch 3-fold repetition and the 40-turn no-mill draw rule; if we are ahead, avoid repeating positions; if behind, repeat to draw.

Process:
- Captain proposes; team votes. Check viewBoard legal move numbers before playing (placement = point number; move = from*100+to; removal = point of opposing piece).
- Keep posts short; record which opening worked in the next retro.
